Each topic gets a persistent Claude Code session running in tmux; the bridge routes messages in, streams responses back, and keeps sessions warm between turns. Uses Anthropic subscription billing (interactive PTY), not API credits.\n4\t\n5\t---\n6\t\n7\t## How it works\n8\t\n9\tThe system is split into two processes:\n10\t\n11\t**Proxy** — A lightweight container that holds the Telegram bot token, long-polls the Telegram `getUpdates` endpoint, and exposes an internal HTTP API (`/updates`, `/send`, `/edit`, etc.) for the bridge to consume. It holds no session state.\n12\t\n13\t**Bridge** — The stateful brain, running as a systemd service on the bare-metal host. It polls the proxy, manages Claude Code sessions, spawns `claude` inside tmux panes (one pane per forum topic), streams responses back via the proxy, and stores session metadata in a local SQLite database.\n14\t\n15\t**Dashboard** (optional) — A Bubbletea TUI that displays real-time session health, in-flight messages, and cost data over a Unix socket.\n16\t\n17\t### Claude invocation\n18\t\n19\tThe bridge maintains a tmux session named `telegram-bridge`. Each active Telegram forum topic maps to one tmux window. Claude Code is launched with configurable permissions:\n20\t\n21\t```\n22\tclaude <permission_flags> --model <model> [--resume <session_id>]\n23\t```\n24\t\n25\tPermission flags are determined by the group's `permission_mode` setting:\n26\t- `bypassPermissions` → `--dangerously-skip-permissions`\n27\t- `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `dontAsk` → `--permission-mode <mode>`\n28\t\n29\t**Note:** The current implementation always passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` regardless of the stored `permission_mode` (tracked issue). The `permission_mode` is configurable via `/config permission_mode <mode>` or `/permission <mode>`, but does not yet affect runtime behavior.\n30\t\n31\tPanes stay warm between messages (45 s idle threshold). A Claude stop-hook writes the final response to a file that the bridge polls; it falls back to PTY screen-scraping if the hook is not configured. On session ID loss, up to 40 messages of history are prepended from SQLite to restore context.\n32\t\n33\t---\n34\t\n35\t## Features\n36\t\n37\t### Notification modes\n38\t\n39\tPer-topic, configurable via `/notify` or natural language:\n40\t\n41\t| Mode | Behavior |\n42\t|------|----------|\n43\t| `live` (default) | Progressively edits one Telegram message as Claude streams (1 s debounce) |\n44\t| `summary` | Posts a placeholder, edits to the final response only when done |\n45\t| `quiet` | No updates during processing; posts only on completion |\n46\t\n47\t### Natural language intent detection\n48\t\n49\tThe bridge intercepts common phrases before forwarding them to Claude:\n50\t\n51\t- **Cancel:** \"cancel\", \"stop\", \"abort\"\n52\t- **Model switch:** \"use opus\", \"think harder\", \"fast mode\", etc.\n53\t- **Notify mode:** \"stream updates\", \"quiet mode\", etc.\n54\t- **Cost / status queries**\n55\t- **Session control:** \"close session\", \"new session\"\n56\t- **Timeout adjustments**\n57\t\n58\t### Media support\n59\t\n60\t| Type | Handling |\n61\t|------|----------|\n62\t| Photos | Injected as image attachments (10 MB limit) |\n63\t| Voice messages | Transcribed via `whisper` CLI, text prepended to prompt |\n64\t| Audio files (MP3, M4A, FLAC, WAV, OGG) | Same as voice messages |\n65\t| Video / video notes | Keyframes extracted + audio transcribed; both fed to Claude |\n66\t| Documents | Passed as file attachments (50 MB limit) |\n67\t\n68\t### Dispatcher / orchestrator mode\n69\t\n70\tWhen enabled (`/dispatch on`), Claude receives two synthetic tools:\n71\t\n72\t- `spawn_worker` — the bridge spawns a headless Claude instance and injects the result back\n73\t- `update_progress` — posts a status message to the topic immediately\n74\t\n75\t### Self-update\n76\t\n77\tThe bridge checks a configurable remote for new versions on a background interval and applies updates with `/update do`. Update checking can be disabled by setting `UPDATE_INTERVAL_MINUTES=0`.\n78\t\n79\t### Session lifecycle\n80\t\n81\t- One session per `(chat_id, thread_id)` pair\n82\t- Messages arriving during processing are batched in a per-topic queue (32 messages deep)\n83\t- Sessions resume across restarts via `--resume <session_id>`\n84\t- Stale sessions cleaned up automatically (configurable interval and TTL)\n85\t- On close: Claude (Haiku) generates a summary and pins it to the topic\n86\t\n87\t---\n88\t\n89\t## Prerequisites\n90\t\n91\tThe following must be available on the host running the bridge:\n92\t\n93\t- **tmux** — session multiplexer that hosts Claude Code panes\n94\t- **claude** — [Claude Code CLI](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code), logged in with an active Anthropic {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_b08d8ae10e6e40eca6f66a62","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Telegram-Claude Bridge: Implementation Plan\n2\t\n3\t## Overview\n4\t\n5\tA two-component system where the bridge acts as a **dispatcher** — routing Telegram conversations to headless Claude Code CLI instances and coordinating their results back to the thread. The bridge is not a pipe; it is an orchestrator of Claude processes.\n6\t\n7\tEach Telegram forum topic maps to an **orchestrator** Claude session: a persistent, resumed `claude` interactive process that understands the user's intent, delegates parallelisable sub-tasks to **worker** instances, and synthesises responses. Workers are short-lived, fresh-session Claude processes spawned by the orchestrator and managed by the bridge. The bridge routes worker results back to both the Telegram thread and the orchestrator's context.\n8\t\n9\tA lightweight proxy on ardenone-cluster isolates the Telegram bot token. The bridge on Hetzner EX44 handles all dispatch logic, session management, worker lifecycle, media processing, and state persistence.\n10\t\n11\t```\n12\tTelegram API  <--token-->  Proxy (ardenone-cluster)  <--Tailscale-->  Bridge (EX44) [dispatcher]\n13\t                                                                              │\n14\t                                                             ┌────────────────┴────────────────┐\n15\t                                                             │                                 │\n16\t                                                      Orchestrator Claude              Worker Claude(s)\n17\t                                                      (resumed session)                (fresh sessions)\n18\t                                                      understands + delegates          execute sub-tasks\n19\t                                                      synthesises + responds           report results back\n20\t```\n21\t\n22\t---\n23\t\n24\t## Component 1: Proxy (ardenone-cluster)\n25\t\n26\t### Purpose\n27\t\n28\tHold the Telegram bot token and act as a dumb authenticated pipe. No routing, no state, no interpretation of message content.\n29\t\n30\t### Technology\n31\t\n32\t- **Language:** Go (same as bridge — shared module, single build system)\n33\t- **Runtime:** Single-container Deployment in its own namespace on ardenone-cluster\n34\t- **Networking:** Tailscale sidecar or host networking for Tailscale access; no public ingress\n35\t\n36\t### Telegram Communication\n37\t\n38\tThe proxy long-polls Telegram using `getUpdates` with:\n39\t- `timeout=30` (long-poll interval)\n40\t- `offset` tracking (last `update_id + 1`)\n41\t- `allowed_updates` filter to reduce noise (only `message`, `edited_message`, `callback_query`, `my_chat_member`, and forum topic service messages)\n42\t\n43\tLong-polling chosen over webhooks because:\n44\t- No public IP or HTTPS endpoint needed\n45\t- Auto-recovers from transient network failures\n46\t- Simpler deployment (no TLS cert management)\n47\t\n48\t### Proxy HTTP API\n49\t\n50\tExposed only over Tailscale. No authentication on the proxy API itself — Tailscale ACLs restrict access to the EX44 node.\n51\t\n52\t#### Inbound (Telegram → Bridge)\n53\t\n54\t```\n55\tGET /updates?timeout=30\n56\t```\n57\t\n58\tReturns a JSON array of pending Telegram updates, stripped of any auth context. The proxy translates each Telegram Update object into a normalized envelope:\n59\t\n60\t```json\n61\t{\n62\t  \"update_id\": 123456789,\n63\t  \"type\": \"message\",\n64\t  \"chat_id\": -1001234567890,\n65\t  \"thread_id\": 42,\n66\t  \"from_user_id\": 789,\n67\t  \"message_id\": 1001,\n68\t  \"timestamp\": 1712169600,\n69\t  \"content\": {\n70\t    \"text\": \"refactor the error handling\",\n71\t    \"entities\": [...]\n72\t  },\n73\t  \"media\": [],\n74\t  \"reply_to_message_id\": null,\n75\t  \"service\": null\n76\t}\n77\t```\n78\t\n79\tFor media messages, the proxy downloads the file from Telegram (using the token) and either:\n80\t- **Option A:** Streams the file bytes in the response (for small files <5MB)\n81\t- **Option B:** Saves to a shared volume or returns a proxy-local URL the bridge can fetch\n82\t\n83\t```\n84\tGET /file/<file_id>\n85\t```\n86\t\n87\tReturns the raw file bytes. The bridge never constructs a Telegram file URL (which would require the token).\n88\t\n89\t#### Outbound (Bridge → Telegram)\n90\t\n91\t```\n92\tPOST /send\n93\t{\n94\t  \"chat_id\": -1001234567890,\n95\t  \"thread_id\": 42,\n96\t  \"text\": \"Here's the refactored code...\",\n97\t  \"parse_mode\": \"HTML\",\n98\t  \"reply_to_message_id\": 1001\n99\t}\n100\t\n101\tPOST /send_photo\n102\tPOST /send_document\n103\tPOST /send_video\n104\tPOST /send_audio\n105\t```\n106\t\n107\tEach accepts a JSON body with chat routing fields. Media endpoints accept multipart form data. The proxy injects the bot token and forwards to the Telegram Bot API. Returns the Telegram API response (including `message_id` for subsequent edits).\n108\t\n109\t```\n110\tPOST /edit\n111\t{\n112\t  \"chat_id\": -1001234567890,\n113\t  \"message_id\": 2001,\n114\t  \"text\": \"Updated streaming response...\",\n115\t  \"parse_mode\": \"HTML\"\n116\t}\n117\t```\n118\t\n119\tFor progressive streaming updates via `editMessageText`.\n120\t\n121\t#### Topic Management (Bridge → Telegram)\n122\t\n123\t```\n124\tPOST /create_topic\n125\t{ \"chat_id\": ..., \"name\": \"...\", \"icon_color\": 7322096 }\n126\t\n127\tPOST /close_topic\n128\t{ \"chat_id\": ..., \"thread_id\": ... }\n129\t\n130\tPOST /reopen_topic\n131\t{ \"chat_id\": ..., \"thread_id\": ... }\n132\t\n133\tPOST /edit_topic\n134\t{ \"chat_id\": ..., \"thread_id\": ..., \"name\": \"...\", \"icon_color\": ... }\n135\t```\n136\t\n137\tThin wrappers around `createForumTopic`, `closeForumTopic`, `reopenForumTopic`, `editForumTopic`.\n138\t\n139\t#### Callback Queries\n140\t\n141\t```\n142\tPOST /answer_callback\n143\t{ \"callback_query_id\": \"...\", \"text\": \"Approved\" }\n144\t```\n145\t\n146\tFor responding to inline keyboard button presses.\n147\t\n148\t### Token Storage\n149\t\n150\tToken fetched from ExternalSecret-managed Kubernetes Secret at pod startup, held only in memory. Never written to disk, never in the pod spec or environment variable literals in manifests.\n151\t\n152\tExternalSecret in `declarative-config/k8s/ardenone-cluster/telegram-bridge/external-secret.yml` references the bot token secret. The Secret object is managed by the cluster's external secret operator and synced to the pod at runtime.\n153\t\n154\t### Deployment\n155\t\n156\t- Namespace: `telegram-bridge` on ardenone-cluster\n157\t- Manifests in `declarative-config` repo under `k8s/ardenone-cluster/telegram-bridge/`\n158\t- ArgoCD Application for GitOps sync\n159\t- Resource limits: 64Mi memory, 100m CPU (this is a tiny workload)\n160\t- Health check: `GET /health` returns 200 if Telegram polling is active\n161\t- Single replica (no HA needed — bridge handles reconnection)\n162\t\n163\t---\n164\t\n165\t## Component 2: Bridge (Hetzner EX44)\n166\t\n167\t### Purpose\n168\t\n169\tThe bridge is the dispatcher and message bus. It routes Telegram messages to the correct orchestrator session, intercepts synthetic tool calls from the orchestrator stream (`spawn_worker`, `update_progress`) to manage worker lifecycles, routes worker results back to the thread and to the orchestrator's context, and handles all state, media, and formatting. No Claude logic runs in the bridge itself — it only manages processes and routes data.\n170\t\n171\t### Technology\n172\t\n173\t- **Language:** Go\n174\t- **HTTP:** stdlib `net/http` for client to proxy\n175\t- **Claude integration:** Interactive Claude CLI via PTY, one tmux pane per active topic. Each session runs `claude --resume <session_id>` in a persistent tmux pane within the `telegram-bridge` session. Prompts are injected via tmux bracketed paste mode (`tmux paste-buffer -p`); responses are extracted **primarily via a stop-hook mechanism** (Claude's `--stop-hook` writes final response to `$BRIDGE_RESPONSE_FILE` which the bridge polls atomically via a `.ready` sentinel file) with **tmux capture-pane screen scraping** as fallback. Billing uses subscription (not API credits) because `claude` runs in a real TTY context, not headless `-p` mode.\n176\t- **Media processing:** `whisper` CLI for audio transcription, `ffmpeg` CLI for video frame/audio extraction (both invoked as subprocesses)\n177\t- **State:** SQLite via `modernc.org/sqlite` (pure Go, no CGo)\n178\t- **Runtime:** single static binary, systemd unit on EX44\n179\t\n180\t### Architecture\n181\t\n182\t```\n183\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n184\t│                          Bridge (EX44) — Dispatcher /send   │  │  Detector     │               │\n218\t│  │  Whisper     │  │  POST /edit   │  │  (NL parsing) │               │\n219\t│  │  ffmpeg      │  │  POST /send_* │  │               │ Breakdown\n225\t\n226\t#### 1. Poller\n227\t\n228\tPolls the proxy's `/updates` endpoint in a loop. Maintains its own long-poll timeout matching the proxy's Telegram poll. On connection failure, retries with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 30s). Deserializes update envelopes and dispatches to the Router.\n229\t\n230\t```go\n231\tfunc pollLoop(ctx context.Context, proxyURL string, router *Router) {\n232\t    backoff := time.Second\n233\t    for {\n234\t        updates, err := fetchUpdates(ctx, proxyURL, 35*time.Second)\n235\t        if err != nil {\n236\t            time.Sleep(backoff)\n237\t            backoff = min(backoff*2, 30*time.Second)\n238\t            continue\n239\t        }\n240\t        backoff = time.Second\n241\t        for _, update := range updates {\n242\t            router.Route(ctx, update)\n243\t        }\n244\t    }\n245\t}\n246\t```\n247\t\n248\t#### 2. Router\n249\t\n250\tLooks up `(chat_id, thread_id)` in the SQLite routing table:\n251\t\n252\t- **General topic (thread_id == 1 or None):** dispatch to Command Handler\n253\t- **Known topic:** dispatch to Session Manager with existing session\n254\t- **Unknown topic:** create new session via Session Manager, register in routing table\n255\t- **Callback queries:** dispatch to the session that sent the inline keyboard\n256\t- **Service messages** (`forum_topic_closed`, `forum_topic_reopened`, `forum_topic_created`): dispatch to Topic Lifecycle handler\n257\t\n258\t#### 3. Session Manager\n259\t\n260\tThe Session Manager implements the dispatcher pattern. It manages two categories of Claude CLI process per topic:\n261\t\n262\t**Orchestrator** — the on-demand, resumed session for a topic. Spawns a tmux pane within the `telegram-bridge` session only when a message arrives. After the response is complete, a short idle timer (`pane_idle_ttl`, default 5 min) keeps the pane warm for follow-up messages. When the timer expires the pane is killed; the `session_id` persists in SQLite so the next message resumes the conversation via `--resume`. Understands user intent, decides what to delegate, posts progress updates, and synthesises the final response.\n263\t\n264\t**Worker** — a short-lived, fresh-session process dispatched by the orchestrator via the `spawn_worker` synthetic tool. Also runs in its own tmux pane, torn down immediately on completion. Executes one concrete sub-task (research, code generation, analysis, etc.). Multiple workers can run in parallel across panes. Results are posted to the thread immediately and injected back into the orchestrator's context on the next turn.\n265\t\n266\t**Pane lifecycle (dynamic load/unload):**\n267\t\n268\t```\n269\tMessage arrives for topic\n270\t        │\n271\t        ▼\n272\tPane alive for topic?\n273\t   ├── Yes (warm)  → inject prompt via PTY write immediately\n274\t   └── No  (cold) → spawn pane:\n275\t                     tmux new-window -t telegram-bridge -n \"topic-<thread_id>\"\n276\t                       \"claude --resume <session_id>\n277\t                               --dangerously-skip-permissions\n278\t                               --model <topic_model>\n279\t                               --cwd <project_dir>\n280\t                               --append-system-prompt '<dispatcher context>'\n281\t                               --stop-hook scripts/bridge-stop-hook.sh\"\n282\t                     wait for startup handshake (~3s: DA query + trust dismiss + ready)\n283\t                     inject prompt via bracketed paste\n284\t\n285\tResponse extracted\n286\t        │\n287\t        ▼\n288\tReset idle timer (pane_idle_ttl = 5 min)\n289\t        │\n290\t        ▼  (timer fires with no new message)\n291\ttmux kill-pane  →  pane_state = idle  (session_id kept in SQLite)\n292\t```\n293\t\n294\tCold-start latency is ~3–4s (claude startup + PTY handshake). Warm injection is near-instant. The `pane_idle_ttl` is configurable per group — set higher for active development sessions, lower for rarely-used topics.\n295\t\n296\t**Worker invocation (transient tmux pane, spawned on spawn_worker tool call):**\n297\t\n298\t```\n299\t# Fresh pane per worker, torn down on completion\n300\ttmux new-window -t telegram-bridge -n \"worker-<worker_id>\" \\\n301\t  \"claude --dangerously-skip-permissions \\\n302\t          --model <worker_model_or_default> \\\n303\t          --cwd <project_dir> \\\n304\t          --disallowed-tools spawn_worker\"\n305\t\n306\t# Prompt injected via bracketed paste; result extracted via stop-hook file or tmux capture-pane\n307\t# Pane closed after result captured\n308\t```\n309\t\n310\tWorkers do not get `--resume` (fresh session each time) and cannot call `spawn_worker` (depth limit = 1).\n311\t\n312\t**Key CLI flags and PTY mechanics:**\n313\t- Interactive mode (no `-p`) — claude runs in REPL mode, billing via subscription\n314\t- `--resume <session_id>` — orchestrator only; restores full conversation context across pane restarts\n315\t- `--append-system-prompt` — injects dispatcher context into orchestrator (see Phase 9)\n316\t- `--disallowed-tools spawn_worker` — workers cannot recursively spawn\n317\t- `--model` — per-session or per-worker model override\n318\t- `--allowed-tools` / `--disallowed-tools` — tool restrictions per group\n319\t- `--stop-hook scripts/bridge-stop-hook.sh` — writes final response to `$BRIDGE_RESPONSE_FILE` for authoritative extraction\n320\t- **Response extraction (primary):** Stop-hook file polling — the stop-hook reads Claude's transcript JSONL, extracts the last assistant message, writes atomically to `.tmp` → rename → touches `.ready`. The bridge polls `.ready` and reads the file.\n321\t- **Response extraction (fallback):** tmux capture-pane — if stop-hook fails or no file produced, bridge scrapes screen via `tmux capture-pane -p -t <paneTarget>`.\n322\t- Bracketed paste mode (`\\x1b[200~` … `\\x1b[201~`) — injects multi-line prompts without triggering premature submission\n323\t- `PRE_RESP_TIMEOUT = 120s` — wait for first `●` after prompt injection\n324\t- `IDLE_TIMEOUT = 45s` — session considered done after 45s silence past last response chunk\n325\t\n326\t**Synthetic tools intercepted by the bridge** (not real Anthropic tools — described via system prompt):\n327\t\n328\t| Tool | Bridge action |\n329\t|---|---|\n330\t| `spawn_worker(prompt, model?)` | Insert workers row, spawn goroutine, return `{worker_id, status: \"dispatched\"}` immediately |\n331\t| `update_progress(message)` | POST message to thread, return `{ok: true}` immediately |\n332\t\n333\tThe scanner loop in `invokeClaudeAPI` intercepts `tool_use` blocks with these names before they reach the `result` event, handles them synchronously (DB write + goroutine spawn), and writes the `tool_result` back to the subprocess stdin so the orchestrator continues without stalling.\n334\t\n335\t**PTY output parsing:**\n336\t- Response start detected by `●` (U+25CF) sentinel in PTY byte stream\n337\t- Tool use detected by watching for known tool-start patterns in the VT100 screen buffer (tmux capture-pane fallback)\n338\t- Response end detected by `────` separator bars and subsequent idle gap\n339\t- **Primary extraction:** Stop-hook file (`$BRIDGE_RESPONSE_FILE.ready` signals completion, file contains last assistant message)\n340\t- **Fallback extraction:** tmux capture-pane screen scraping if stop-hook fails\n341\t- Session ID captured from the initial pane startup output (claude prints it on attach/resume)\n342\t- Cost/usage tracked via `cost_events` table with per-message token counts (from Claude stop-hook transcript)\n343\t\n344\t**Worker goroutine on completion:**\n345\t1. Update `workers` row: `status=done`, `result=...`, `finished_at=now`\n346\t2. Post to thread: `⚙️ Worker [N] done: <truncated result>`\n347\t3. Append to `SessionManager.pendingWorkerResults[(chatID,threadID)]`\n348\t\n349\t**Next orchestrator prompt construction:**\n350\t```\n351\t[Worker results available]\n352\tWorker 1 (<model>): <result>\n353\tWorker 2 (<model>): error — <error>\n354\t\n355\t[User message]\n356\t<user text>\n357\t```\n358\t\n359\tThe `pendingWorkerResults` map is drained atomically at the start of each `processBatch`.\n360\t\n361\t**Orchestrator session lifecycle:**\n362\t- **Create:** First message to a new topic — launch pane (no `--resume`), capture `session_id` from startup output, store in SQLite, start idle timer\n363\t- **Warm resume:** Message arrives while pane is alive — inject prompt directly, reset idle timer\n364\t- **Cold resume:** Message arrives after pane was culled — relaunch with `--resume <session_id>`, wait for startup handshake, inject prompt, start idle timer\n365\t- **Idle cull:** `pane_idle_ttl` expires — `tmux kill-pane`, set `pane_state=idle`; `session_id` retained in SQLite\n366\t- **Close:** `/close`, topic deletion, or natural language close intent — `tmux kill-pane`, mark `status=closed` in SQLite; session permanently ended\n367\t\n368\t**Concurrency model:**\n369\t- One orchestrator goroutine per topic (non-blocking worker, messages buffer in `pending` slice)\n370\t- N worker goroutines per topic (parallel, bounded by `groups.max_workers`)\n371\t- Workers post to thread and inject context independently of the orchestrator\n372\t\n373\t**Timeout:**\n374\t- Orchestrator: `groups.timeout_sec` (default 1800s), `0` = no deadline\n375\t- Workers: inherit group default; can be overridden per `spawn_worker` call\n376\t- Bridge-side progress ticker fires every `groups.progress_interval_sec` (default 120s) if no output sent\n377\t\n378\t```go\n379\t// PTY read loop with timeout\n380\tselect {\n381\tcase resp := <-ptyResponseCh:\n382\t    // response extracted from stop-hook file or tmux capture-pane\n383\tcase <-time.After(timeout):\n384\t    // kill the pane, notify user in Telegram\n385\t    tmuxKillPane(paneID)\n386\t}\n387\t```\n388\t\n389\t**File/image attachments:** Files downloaded from the proxy are saved to a temp directory and referenced in the prompt text. Claude Code's `Read` tool can process images, PDFs, code files, and notebooks from the filesystem. The prompt includes the file path:\n390\t\n391\t```\n392\t[User sent an image: /tmp/telegram-bridge/12345/photo.jpg]\n393\tPlease analyze this screenshot.\n394\t```\n395\t\n396\tClaude Code will use its `Read` tool to open the file.\n397\t\n398\t#### 4. Media Processor\n399\t\n400\tHandles non-text message types before they reach Claude.\n401\t\n402\t**Images:**\n403\t- Download from proxy via `GET /file/<file_id>`\n404\t- Resize to ~800px on the long edge (save tokens, ~1334 tokens per 1000x1000)\n405\t- Save to `/tmp/telegram-bridge/<chat_id>/<message_id>.jpg`\n406\t- Reference in prompt text so Claude Code's `Read` tool can open it\n407\t\n408\t**Voice/Audio:**\n409\t- Download from proxy\n410\t- Transcribe via Whisper (`whisper --model turbo --output_format txt`)\n411\t- Prepend transcription to the text prompt: `[Voice message transcription]: <text>`\n412\t- Retain original audio path for reference\n413\t\n414\t**Video:**\n415\t- Download from proxy\n416\t- Extract keyframes: `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vf \"fps=0.5,scale=800:-1\" frame_%04d.jpg`\n417\t- Extract audio track: `ffmpeg -i video.mp4 -vn -acodec pcm_s16le audio.wav`\n418\t- Transcribe audio via Whisper\n419\t- Combine: attach keyframes as images + prepend audio transcription as text\n420\t\n421\t**Documents:**\n422\t- Download from proxy\n423\t- If Claude-compatible (text, code, PDF, images, notebooks): save to temp dir, reference path in prompt\n424\t- If incompatible (Office docs, archives): attempt conversion or notify user of limitation\n425\t\n426\t**Cleanup:** Temp files cleaned up after session processes the message. Configurable retention for debugging.\n427\t\n428\t#### 5. Command Handler\n429\t\n430\tProcesses bot commands. Commands are recognized in both the General topic and non-General topics, but the available commands differ by context.\n431\t\n432\t**General topic commands (group-level):**\n433\t\n434\t| Command | Action |\n435\t|---|---|\n436\t| `/status` | List active sessions in this group with last activity time |\n437\t| `/sessions` | List all sessions across all groups |\n438\t| `/cwd [path]` | View or set the default working directory for this group |\n439\t| `/new [name]` | Create a new topic and Claude session |\n440\t| `/close [topic]` | Close a topic and optionally end its Claude session |\n441\t| `/model [name]` | View or set the default model for this group |\n442\t| `/timeout [seconds]` | View or set the prompt timeout for this group |\n443\t| `/budget [usd]` | View or set the max budget per session for this group |\n444\t| `/cost` | Show cost breakdown (group total / daily trend / per-topic / per-user) |\n445\t| `/help` | Show available commands |\n446\t| `/ping` | Health check — responds with latency to proxy and Claude |\n447\t| `/version` | Show bridge and proxy versions (semver + commit hash) |\n448\t| `/update` | (admin) Trigger self-update check and apply if available |\n449\t\n450\t**Topic commands (session-level):**\n451\t\n452\t| Command | Action |\n453\t|---|---|\n454\t| `/model [name]` | View or set the model for this topic. Overrides group default. |\n455\t| `/haiku` | Shortcut: set this topic to `claude-haiku-4-5` |\n456\t| `/sonnet` | Shortcut: set this topic to `claude-sonnet-4-6` |\n457\t| `/opus` | Shortcut: set this topic to `claude-opus-4-6` |\n458\t| `/color [name]` | Set topic icon color (`active`, `complete`, `blocked`, `error`, `review`, `research`) |\n459\t| `/notify [mode]` | Set notification mode (`live`, `summary`, `quiet`) |\n460\t| `/context <thread_id>` | Inject context from another topic into this session |\n461\t| `/snippet <name> <content>` | Save a named context snippet |\n462\t| `/snippets` | List saved snippets |\n463\t| `/info` | Show session info: model, cwd, session_id, cost, message count, notify mode, timeout |\n464\t| `/dispatch [on|off|default]` | Toggle orchestrator mode |\n465\t| `/timeout [N]` | Set per-topic timeout in seconds (0 = use group default) |\n466\t| `/cancel` | Cancel the running request |\n467\t| `/parallel <prompts>` | Run up to 5 prompts in parallel (separate with `---`) |\n468\t| `/bg <command>` | Run a shell command in the background and stream output to the topic |\n469\t| `/jobs` | List background jobs |\n470\t| `/kill <job_id>` | Kill a background job |\n471\t\n472\tAll other text in non-General topics is passed through to Claude as the prompt — but the bridge scans it for intent first (model switching, cancel, notify mode, cost queries, session control, timeout adjustments) via natural language intent detection.\n473\t\n474\t**Natural language intent detection:**\n475\t\n476\tThe bridge intercepts common phrases before forwarding them to Claude:\n477\t\n478\t- **Cancel:** \"cancel\", \"stop\", \"abort\", \"never mind\", \"scratch that\"\n479\t- **Model switch:** \"use opus\", \"think harder\", \"fast mode\", \"switch to sonnet\", \"back to default\"\n480\t- **Notify mode:** \"stream updates\", \"quiet mode\", \"just tell me when done\", \"no updates\"\n481\t- **Cost / status queries:** \"how much\", \"show cost\", \"what is the cost\", \"total cost\", \"show status\", \"session info\"\n482\t- **Session control:** \"close session\", \"end session\", \"we are done\", \"all done\", \"wrap up\"\n483\t- **Timeout adjustments:** \"give me more time\", \"extend timeout\"\n484\t\n485\tImplementation: `strings.ToLower()` then `strings.Contains()` against a table of known phrases. No regex. The phrases are deliberately specific — a verb of intent (\"use\", \"switch to\", \"need\") paired with a model name or tier keyword — so the detector doesn't misfire on messages that happen to contain \"opus\" in a different context.\n486\t\n487\t**Model resolution order:** The bridge resolves which model to use for each CLI invocation in this order (first non-null wins):\n488\t\n489\t1. `sessions.model` — topic-level override (set via `/model`, `/haiku`, `/sonnet`, `/opus`, or natural language in the topic)\n490\t2. `groups.default_model` — group-level default (set via `/model` in General topic)\n491\t3. Hardcoded fallback: `claude-sonnet-4-6`\n492\t\n493\tWhen a topic-level model is set, the bridge updates the pinned metadata message to reflect the current model.\n494\t\n495\t#### 6. Response Formatter\n496\t\n497\tConverts Claude's output to Telegram-compatible format.\n498\t\n499\t**Markdown → HTML conversion:**\n500\t- Claude outputs markdown; Telegram needs HTML (chosen over MarkdownV2 for reliability)\n501\t- Convert: `**bold**` → `<b>`, `*italic*` → `<i>`, `` `code` `` → `<code>`, code fences → `<pre><code class=\"language-X\">`, `[text](url)` → `<a href=\"url\">text</a>`\n502\t- Escape `<`, `>`, `&` in plain text\n503\t- Strip unsupported markdown features gracefully\n504\t\n505\t**Message chunking:**\n506\t- Telegram limit: 4096 characters per message\n507\t- Split at natural boundaries in priority order: paragraph breaks, code block boundaries, sentence endings\n508\t- Never split inside a code block — if a code block exceeds 4096 chars, send it as a document attachment instead\n509\t- First chunk is a reply to the user's message; subsequent chunks are standalone in the same topic\n510\t\n511\t**Streaming (progressive updates):**\n512\t- Send initial \"Thinking...\" placeholder message\n513\t- Edit the message with new content as Claude streams (debounce: max 1 edit/second to stay under Telegram rate limits)\n514\t- On completion, send final formatted message (replacing the streamed version if formatting differs)\n515\t- If response exceeds 4096 chars during streaming, stop editing and send new messages for overflow\n516\t\n517\t**Notification modes:**\n518\t\n519\tPer-topic, configurable via `/notify` or natural language (\"stream updates\", \"quiet mode\", etc.):\n520\t\n521\t| Mode | Behavior |\n522\t|------|----------|\n523\t| `live` (default) | Progressively edits one Telegram message as Claude streams (1 s debounce) |\n524\t| `summary` | Posts a placeholder, edits to the final response only when done |\n525\t| `quiet` | No updates during processing; posts only on completion |\n526\t\n527\t#### 7. Sender\n528\t\n529\tThin async HTTP client that posts to the proxy's outbound endpoints. Handles:\n530\t- Rate limiting: respect Telegram's 1 msg/sec per chat, 20 msg/min per group, ~30 global\n531\t- Retry on 429 with `retry_after` from Telegram\n532\t- Retry on proxy connection failure with exponential backoff\n533\t- Response tracking: store `message_id` of sent messages for subsequent edits\n534\t\n535\t#### 8. Intent Detector\n536\t\n537\tNatural language intent recognition (test-driven examples) that intercepts common user phrases before forwarding to Claude:\n538\t\n539\t- `detectCancelIntent()` — cancel phrases: \"cancel\", \"stop\", \"abort\", \"never mind\", \"scratch that\"\n540\t- `detectModelChange()` — model switching: \"use opus\", \"switch to sonnet\", \"back to default\", tier escalation (\"think harder\"), de-escalation (\"keep it simple\")\n541\t- `detectNotifyIntent()` — notification mode: \"quiet\", \"silent\", \"just tell me when done\" → summary; \"be quiet\", \"no updates\" → quiet; \"show everything\", \"keep me posted\" → live\n542\t- `detectCostIntent()` — cost queries: \"how much\", \"what is the cost\", \"show cost\", \"total cost\"\n543\t- `detectStatusIntent()` — status queries: \"what are you doing\", \"show status\", \"session info\", \"are you busy\"\n544\t- `detectCloseIntent()` — session control: \"close this session\", \"end session\", \"we are done\", \"all done\", \"wrap up\"\n545\t- `detectTimeoutIntent()` — timeout adjustments: \"give me more time\", \"extend timeout\"\n546\t\n547\t#### 9. State (SQLite)\n548\t\n549\t```sql\n550\t-- Current schema version: 24\n551\t-- Migrations are applied sequentially on startup; schema_version prevents re-application.\n552\t\n553\t-- Which groups are registered and their default settings\n554\tCREATE TABLE groups (\n555\t    chat_id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n556\t    name                    TEXT,\n557\t    cwd                     TEXT NOT NULL,\n558\t    default_model           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'claude-sonnet-4-6',\n559\t    max_budget              REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 5.0,\n560\t    timeout_sec             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1800,\n561\t    permission_mode         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'acceptEdits',  -- Stored but not wired to CLI flags (see Security section)\n562\t    allowed_tools           TEXT,                              -- JSON array of tool names\n563\t    disallowed_tools        TEXT,                              -- JSON array of tool names\n564\t    max_subtasks            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,        -- Max concurrent /parallel subtasks\n565\t    max_workers             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5,        -- Max concurrent spawn_worker\n566\t    progress_interval_sec   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 120,      -- Progress ticker (0 = disabled)\n567\t    dispatcher_mode         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,        -- 1 = orchestrator mode, 0 = direct\n568\t    transcript_verify       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,        -- 1 = require approval for audio transcription\n569\t    created_at              TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n570\t);\n571\t\n572\t-- Maps each topic to a Claude Code session\n573\tCREATE TABLE sessions (\n574\t    chat_id               INTEGER NOT NULL,\n575\t    thread_id             INTEGER NOT NULL,\n576\t    session_id            TEXT NOT NULL,\n577\t    cwd                   TEXT NOT NULL,\n578\t    model                 TEXT,\n579\t    status                TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',      -- active, closed, error\n580\t    icon_color            INTEGER,                              -- Topic icon color code\n581\t    created_at            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n582\t    last_active           TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n583\t    message_count         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n584\t    pinned_message_id     INTEGER,                              -- Metadata message pinned in topic\n585\t    total_cost_usd        REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0.0,\n586\t    summary               TEXT,                                  -- Session summary generated on close\n587\t    notification_mode     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'live',         -- live, summary, quiet\n588\t    timeout_sec           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,           -- Per-topic timeout override\n589\t    dispatcher_mode       INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT -1,          -- 1 = enabled, 0 = disabled, -1 = use group default\n590\t    topic_name            TEXT,                                  -- Forum topic name for /context lookup\n591\t    last_from_user_id     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,           -- Last Telegram user to message this session\n592\t    PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, thread_id),\n593\t    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id) REFERENCES groups(chat_id)\n594\t);\n595\t\n596\t-- Authorized Telegram user IDs\n597\tCREATE TABLE allowed_users (\n598\t    user_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n599\t    role          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'user',      -- admin, user\n600\t    added_at      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n601\t);\n602\t\n603\t-- Tracks sent message IDs for edit-in-place streaming and deduplication\n604\tCREATE TABLE sent_messages (\n605\t    chat_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,\n606\t    thread_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,\n607\t    message_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,\n608\t    purpose       TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- streaming, response, command, placeholder\n609\t    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n610\t    PRIMARY KEY (chat_id, thread_id, message_id)\n611\t);\n612\t\n613\t-- Cost tracking per API invocation (from Claude stop-hook transcript)\n614\tCREATE TABLE cost_events (\n615\t    id                    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n616\t    chat_id               INTEGER NOT NULL,\n617\t    thread_id             INTEGER NOT NULL,\n618\t    cost_usd              REAL NOT NULL,\n619\t    input_tokens          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n620\t    output_tokens         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n621\t    cache_read_tokens     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n622\t    cache_creation_tokens INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n623\t    model                 TEXT NOT NULL,\n624\t    from_user_id          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,\n625\t    created_at            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n626\t    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id, thread_id) REFERENCES sessions(chat_id, thread_id)\n627\t);\n628\t\n629\t-- Parallel subtasks spawned by /parallel or SubtaskOrchestrator\n630\tCREATE TABLE subtasks (\n631\t    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                    -- UUID\n632\t    chat_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,\n633\t    thread_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,\n634\t    parent_msg    INTEGER,                              -- Message ID that spawned this subtask\n635\t    prompt        TEXT NOT NULL,\n636\t    session_id    TEXT,                                  -- Optional session_id to resume\n637\t    status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',      -- running, complete, error\n638\t    result        TEXT,\n639\t    error         TEXT,\n640\t    started_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n641\t    finished_at   TEXT,\n642\t    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id, thread_id) REFERENCES sessions(chat_id, thread_id)\n643\t);\n644\t\n645\t-- Worker processes spawned via spawn_worker synthetic tool\n646\tCREATE TABLE workers (\n647\t    id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                      -- UUID\n648\t    chat_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,\n649\t    thread_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,\n650\t    parent_msg   INTEGER NOT NULL,\n651\t    prompt       TEXT NOT NULL,\n652\t    session_id   TEXT,\n653\t    model        TEXT,\n654\t    status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',      -- running, done, failed\n655\t    result       TEXT,\n656\t    error        TEXT,\n657\t    started_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n658\t    finished_at  TEXT,\n659\t    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id, thread_id) REFERENCES sessions(chat_id, thread_id)\n660\t);\n661\t\n662\t-- Background shell jobs spawned via /bg\n663\tCREATE TABLE background_jobs (\n664\t    id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,                       -- 8-character hex\n665\t    chat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,\n666\t    thread_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,\n667\t    command     TEXT NOT NULL,\n668\t    status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',       -- running, complete, error, interrupted\n669\t    exit_code   INTEGER,\n670\t    started_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n671\t    finished_at TEXT,\n672\t    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id, thread_id) REFERENCES sessions(chat_id, thread_id)\n673\t);\n674\t\n675\t-- Reusable context snippets for a chat\n676\tCREATE TABLE snippets (\n677\t    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY UNIQUE(chat_id, name),\n683\t    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id) REFERENCES groups(chat_id)\n684\t);\n685\t\n686\t-- Conversation messages stored for session restore on loss\n687\tCREATE TABLE conversation_messages (\n688\t    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,\n689\t    chat_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,\n690\t    thread_id  INTEGER NOT NULL,\n691\t    role       TEXT NOT NULL,                            -- user, assistant\n692\t    content    TEXT NOT NULL,\n693\t    tg_msg_id  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,              -- Telegram message ID (0 for assistant)\n694\t    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n695\t    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id, thread_id) REFERENCES sessions(chat_id, thread_id)\n696\t);\n697\t\n698\t-- Update deduplication for replay prevention after proxy offset loss\n699\tCREATE TABLE processed_updates (\n700\t    update_id   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n701\t    processed_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now'))\n702\t);\n703\t```\n704\t\n705\t### Security\n706\t\n707\t#### User Authorization\n708\t\n709\t- `allowed_users` table is the allowlist. Only messages from authorized `from_user_id` values are processed.\n710\t- Admin role can use `/cwd`, `/model`, `/budget`, `/timeout`, and manage group settings.\n711\t- User role can send messages to topics and use `/status`, `/help`, `/new`, `/close`, and all topic-level commands.\n712\t- Unknown users are silently ignored (no error response to prevent enumeration).\n713\t\n714\t#### Input Handling\n715\t\n716\t- User messages are passed to Claude via stdin pipe to the subprocess, never interpolated into shell commands or CLI arguments.\n717\t- File paths from Telegram are never used directly — files are saved with generated names in a sandboxed temp directory.\n718\t\n719\t#### Claude Code Permissions\n720\t\n721\t- **Default runtime behavior:** Every Claude invocation passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag (effectively `bypassPermissions`). The `permission_mode` is stored in the database (`groups.permission_mode`, `sessions.permission_mode`) but does not affect runtime behavior in the current implementation due to the pervasive skip-permissions flag.\n722\t- **Stored permission modes:** `acceptEdits` (default), `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, `dontAsk` — configurable per group and per topic via `/permission` or `/config permission_mode`, but not wired to CLI flags (tracked open issue).\n723\t- `--allowed-tools` and `--disallowed-tools` are configurable per group to restrict what Claude can do.\n724\t- **Note:** Wiring the stored `permission_mode` value to actual CLI flags is a tracked open issue (see related bead about permission mode integration).\n725\t\n726\t### Topic Lifecycle Management\n727\t\n728\t#### Automatic Registration\n729\t\n730\tWhen the bridge receives a message for an unknown `(chat_id, thread_id)`:\n731\t1. Check if `chat_id` is in the `groups` table. If not, ignore (group must be registered first via `/cwd` in General topic).\n732\t2. Create a new session with a generated session ID.\n733\t3. Insert into `sessions` table with the group's default `cwd` and `model`.\n734\t4. Send an initial context message to Claude including the topic name as task context.\n735\t\n736\t#### Status Tracking via Icon Colors\n737\t\n738\tThe bridge updates topic icon colors to reflect session status:\n739\t\n740\t| Status | Color | Hex |\n741\t|---|---|---|\n742\t| Active (processing) | Light blue | `0x6FB9F0` |\n743\t| Complete (closed) | Green | `0x8EEE98` |\n744\t| Blocked/waiting | Yellow | `0xFFD67E` |\n745\t| Error | Red/orange | `0xFB6F5F` |\n746\t| Review needed | Pink | `0xFF93B2` |\n747\t| Research/exploration | Purple | `0xCB86DB` |\n748\t\n749\tUpdated via `POST /edit_topic` to the proxy when session status changes.\n750\t\n751\t#### Pinned Metadata\n752\t\n753\tOn session creation, the bridge pins a message in the topic:\n754\t\n755\t```\n756\tSession: abc123\n757\tProject: ~/telegram-claude-bridge\n758\tModel: claude-sonnet-4-6 (group default)\n759\tStarted: 2026-04-03 18:30 UTC\n760\t```\n761\t\n762\tUpdated when settings change (including model override via `/model`, `/haiku`, `/sonnet`, `/opus`). When a topic-level model override is active, the pinned message shows:\n763\t\n764\t```\n765\tModel: claude-opus-4-6 (topic override)\n766\t```\n767\t\n768\t#### Close/Reopen\n769\t\n770\t- Topic closed in Telegram → bridge marks session as `closed` in SQLite, optionally frees SDK resources.\n771\t- Topic reopened → bridge marks session as `active`, resumes via `--resume session_id`.\n772\t- `/close` command → bridge closes the topic via proxy (`POST /close_topic`) and marks session closed.\n773\t\n774\t---\n775\t\n776\t## Phase 1: Minimal Viable Bridge\n777\t\n778\tGoal: Send a text message in a Telegram topic, get a Claude response back.\n779\t\n780\t### 1.1 — Telegram Bot Setup\n781\t- Create bot via BotFather\n782\t- Store token in ExternalSecret on ardenone-cluster\n783\t- Create a supergroup with forum mode enabled\n784\t- Grant bot admin with `can_manage_topics`\n785\t\n786\t### 1.2 — Proxy MVP\n787\t- Go binary (`cmd/proxy/main.go`), stdlib `net/http`\n788\t- Long-poll Telegram, expose `/updates`, `/send`, `/edit`, `/health`\n789\t- Token from env var (ExternalSecret injection at pod start)\n790\t- `FROM scratch` container, deploy to ardenone-cluster via ArgoCD\n791\t- Verify: curl from EX44 over Tailscale returns updates\n792\t\n793\t### 1.3 — Bridge MVP\n794\t- Go binary (`cmd/bridge/main.go`)\n795\t- Poller → Router → Session Manager → Sender pipeline\n796\t- SQLite state with `groups` and `sessions` tables (`modernc.org/sqlite`)\n797\t- General topic: `/cwd` command to register a group\n798\t- Non-General topics: create tmux pane + session on first message, inject into existing pane on subsequent\n799\t- PTY manager component: launches/tracks tmux panes in the `telegram-bridge` session (one pane per active topic), injects prompts via bracketed paste, extracts responses via stop-hook file with tmux capture-pane fallback\n800\t- Text-only (no media processing)\n801\t- No streaming initially — wait for full response from stop-hook or PTY, send as single message (chunked if >4096)\n802\t- Single static binary, systemd unit on EX44\n803\t- Verify: send message in topic, receive Claude response\n804\t\n805\t### 1.4 — Basic Commands\n806\t- `/status`, `/help`, `/cwd`, `/sessions` in General topic\n807\t- `/close` to end a session\n808\t- User allowlist (single admin user initially)\n809\t\n810\t**Deliverable:** Working text-in, text-out bridge with topic-based conversation isolation.\n811\t\n812\t---\n813\t\n814\t## Phase 2: Streaming and Formatting\n815\t\n816\t### 2.1 — Progressive Streaming\n817\t- Monitor PTY output while arriving (after `●` sentinel, before end-of-response separator)\n818\t- Extract response text via tmux capture-pane on each poll tick (~300ms)\n819\t- Send placeholder message, edit in-place as new text appears\n820\t- Debounce edits to 1/second\n821\t- Handle overflow (>4096 chars) by sending new messages\n822\t\n823\t### 2.2 — Response Formatting\n824\t- Markdown → HTML converter\n825\t- Code-block-aware message chunking\n826\t- Oversized code blocks sent as document attachments\n827\t\n828\t### 2.3 — Permission Handling\n829\t- **Default runtime behavior:** Every Claude invocation passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag (effectively `bypassPermissions`).\n830\t- The stored `permission_mode` in the database is configurable per group and per topic (`bypassPermissions`, `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `dontAsk`) via `/permission` or `/config permission_mode`, but is not currently wired to CLI flags (tracked open issue).\n831\t- Alternative modes available in storage require manual wiring to affect runtime behavior.\n832\t\n833\t**Deliverable:** Streamed responses with proper formatting.\n834\t\n835\t---\n836\t\n837\t## Phase 3: Media Processing\n838\t\n839\t### 3.1 — Image Support\n840\t- Download photos from proxy\n841\t- Resize to ~800px\n842\t- Pass to Claude as file attachments\n843\t- Send image responses (screenshots, generated diagrams) back via `/send_photo`\n844\t\n845\t### 3.2 — Voice/Audio Support\n846\t- Download voice messages and audio files from proxy\n847\t- Transcribe via Whisper (turbo model)\n848\t- Inject transcription into prompt\n849\t- Send transcription back to user for verification before prompting Claude (opt-in via `groups.transcript_verify`)\n850\t\n851\t### 3.3 — Document Support\n852\t- Download documents from proxy\n853\t- Route to Claude based on file type (text/code/PDF/image → direct, others → notify limitation)\n854\t- Send file responses back via `/send_document`\n855\t\n856\t### 3.4 — Video Support (stretch)\n857\t- Extract keyframes via ffmpeg\n858\t- Extract and transcribe audio\n859\t- Combine into multi-modal prompt\n860\t\n861\t**Deliverable:** Full multi-modal input support — images, voice, documents, and optionally video.\n862\t\n863\t---\n864\t\n865\t## Phase 4: Topic Lifecycle and Operations\n866\t\n867\t### 4.1 — Topic Auto-Creation\n868\t- `/new [name]` command creates a Telegram topic and registers a session\n869\t- Claude can suggest creating a new topic (bridge parses (1.2s, 340 tokens)     ││\n950\t│  │ 09:30:45 ← #trading-bot  claude complete (4.8s, $0.032)             ││\n951\t│  │ 09:30:12 → #trading-bot  @jed \"add stop-loss logic\"                 ││\n952\t│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘│\n953\t│                                                                          │\n954\t│  ┌─ Command Log This hour: $0.12  │  Active: 4      ││\n962\t│ Panels\n967\t\n968\t#### Active Sessions\n969\t- Lists all sessions with status (processing/streaming/idle/error), model, topic name\n970\t- Color-coded: green=idle, blue=processing, yellow=streaming, red=error\n971\t- Shows idle duration for inactive sessions\n972\t- Sorted by last activity (most recent first)\n973\t\n974\t#### System Health\n975\t- Real-time health checks mirroring the bridge's internal health checker\n976\t- Proxy latency, bridge uptime, DB response time, Claude CLI availability\n977\t- Telegram polling status and last update ID\n978\t\n979\t#### Messages In Flight\n980\t- Scrolling log of inbound (→) and outbound (←) messages\n981\t- Shows topic name, user, message preview (truncated to terminal width)\n982\t- For outbound: streaming progress, token count, cost, duration\n983\t- Ring buffer of last ~100 messages\n984\t\n985\t#### Command Log\n986\t- Scrolling log of `/commands` processed by the bridge\n987\t- Shows command, topic, user, result (OK/error)\n988\t- Ring buffer of last ~50 commands\n989\t\n990\t#### Cost Tracker\n991\t- Aggregated cost from session `total_cost_usd` fields\n992\t- Today's total, current hour, and active session count\n993\t- Per-session breakdown available by selecting a session in the Active Sessions panel\n994\t\n995\t### Event Stream\n996\t\n997\tThe bridge publishes events to a local Unix socket at `/tmp/telegram-bridge-events.sock` (or configurable path). The event protocol is NDJSON with event types:\n998\t\n999\t```json\n1000\t{\"type\":\"message_in\",\"timestamp\":\"...\",\"chat_id\":...,\"thread_id\":...,\"topic\":\"#trading-bot\",\"user\":\"@jed\",\"preview\":\"add stop-loss logic\"}\n1001\t{\"type\":\"message_out\",\"timestamp\":\"...\",\"chat_id\":...,\"thread_id\":...,\"topic\":\"#trading-bot\",\"status\":\"streaming\",\"tokens\":340,\"elapsed_ms\":1200}\n1002\t{\"type\":\"message_out\",\"timestamp\":\"...\",\"chat_id\":...,\"thread_id\":...,\"topic\":\"#trading-bot\",\"status\":\"complete\",\"tokens\":1200,\"cost_usd\":0.032,\"elapsed_ms\":4800}\n1003\t{\"type\":\"command\",\"timestamp\":\"...\",\"command\":\"/model\",\"args\":\"opus\",\"topic\":\"#new-feature\",\"user\":\"@jed\",\"result\":\"ok\"}\n1004\t{\"type\":\"session_update\",\"timestamp\":\"...\",\"chat_id\":...,\"thread_id\":...,\"topic\":\"#new-feature\",\"status\":\"active\",\"model\":\"claude-opus-4-6\"}\n1005\t{\"type\":\"health\",\"timestamp\":\"...\",\"proxy_ok\":true,\"proxy_latency_ms\":210,\"db_ok\":true,\"db_latency_ms\":6}\n1006\t```\n1007\t\n1008\tThe bridge emits events regardless of whether the TUI is connected. If no listener is present, writes are silently dropped (non-blocking).\n1009\t\n1010\t### Running\n1011\t\n1012\t```bash\n1013\t# In a tmux session\n1014\ttmux new -s dashboard\n1015\t./bin/dashboard\n1016\t\n1017\t# Or with a custom socket path\n1018\t./bin/dashboard --socket /tmp/telegram-bridge-events.sock\n1019\t```\n1020\t\n1021\tThe dashboard is optional — the bridge functions identically without it. It's a pure observer for operational visibility.\n1022\t\n1023\t**Deliverable:** Real-time terminal dashboard for monitoring bridge activity, session state, and costs.\n1024\t\n1025\t## Phase 7: Foundational Infrastructure for Dispatcher\n1026\t\n1027\t### Purpose\n1028\t\n1029\tPrerequisite pieces that the Phase 8 dispatcher architecture depends on. The bridge must support long-running invocations, cancellation, and non-blocking operation before the orchestrator/worker model can work reliably. Phases 7 and 8 are designed together — Phase 7 is the infrastructure layer, Phase 8 is the dispatch layer built on top of it.\n1030\t\n1031\t**Status of 7.1–7.2:** Implemented (under interactive PTY model). These need revisiting under the interactive PTY model — cancellation now means writing `\\x03` (Ctrl-C) to the pane's PTY rather than sending SIGTERM to a subprocess, and timeout means abandoning the PTY read loop and killing the pane.\n1032\t\n1033\t### 7.1 — In-flight cancellation\n1034\t\n1035\t**Problem:** A stuck or long-running invocation holds the topic PTY read loop with no escape.\n1036\t\n1037\t**Solution:** Track the active pane ID in `topicWorker`. A `/cancel` command writes `\\x03` (Ctrl-C) to the pane's PTY to interrupt the running Claude turn.\n1038\t\n1039\t```go\n1040\ttype topicWorker struct {\n1041\t    ch          chan sessionMsg\n1042\t    cancel      context.CancelFunc\n1043\t    activePaneID string   // guarded by activeMu\n1044\t    activeMu    sync.Mutex\n1045\t}\n1046\t```\n1047\t\n1048\t- Set `activePaneID` when pane is launched; clear it after PTY read loop exits.\n1049\t- `/cancel [thread_id]` command: acquire `activeMu`, write `\\x03` to the pane PTY via `tmux send-keys -t <paneID> C-c`.\n1050\t- Edit the \"Thinking…\" placeholder to \"⚠️ Cancelled\" on cancellation.\n1051\t- Topic color → red on cancel.\n1052\t\n1053\t### 7.2 — Extended timeouts + per-topic timeout override\n1054\t\n1055\t**Problem:** `defaultSessionTimeout = 300` (5 min) is too low for agentic tasks. Per-topic override is missing.\n1056\t\n1057\t**Changes:**\n1058\t- Raise `defaultSessionTimeout` from `300` → `1800` (30 min).\n1059\t- Add `timeout_sec` column to `sessions` table (mirrors `groups.timeout_sec`). Per-topic override takes precedence over group default.\n1060\t- Add `/timeout [N]` as a topic-level command (currently only group-level via `/config`).\n1061\t- `N=0` disables the timeout entirely (no `context.WithTimeout`).\n1062\t- Add `/timeout` to `/help` output.\n1063\t\n1064\t**Timeout resolution order** (first non-zero wins):\n1065\t1. `sessions.timeout_sec` — topic-level override\n1066\t2. `groups.timeout_sec` — group default\n1067\t3. `defaultSessionTimeout` — hardcoded fallback (1800s)\n1068\t\n1069\t### 7.3 — Tool-use progress notifications\n1070\t\n1071\t**Problem:** During long agentic runs the user sees only \"Thinking…\" with no visibility into what Claude is doing.\n1072\t\n1073\t**Solution:** Parse `tool_use` and `tool_result` events from the stream-json NDJSON and send interim status messages to the topic.\n1074\t\n1075\tStream-json emits `stream_event` lines containing `message_delta` and tool events. Parse:\n1076\t```json\n1077\t{\"type\":\"stream_event\",\"event\":{\"type\":\"content_block_start\",\"content_block\":{\"type\":\"tool_use\",\"name\":\"Bash\",\"input\":{\"command\":\"go test ./...\"}}}}\n1078\t```\n1079\t\n1080\tBehavior:\n1081\t- On `tool_use` start: edit the placeholder → `⚙️ Running Bash: \\`go test ./...\\`` (truncated to 100 chars)\n1082\t- On `tool_result`: edit → `✓ Bash done (exit 0)` or `✗ Bash failed (exit 1)`\n1083\t- On final result: replace with full streamed response as now\n1084\t- Debounce tool notifications at 500ms (faster than text streaming since these are discrete events)\n1085\t- Long tool commands truncated in the notification but full output still goes to Claude\n1086\t\n1087\t### 7.4 — Sub-task orchestrator (multi-instance fan-out/fan-in)\n1088\t\n1089\t**Core feature:** Allow Claude or the user to dispatch multiple parallel interactive Claude instances (each in its own tmux pane) from a single topic, with results funneled back to that topic.\n1090\t\n1091\t#### SQLite schema addition\n1092\t\n1093\t```sql\n1094\tCREATE TABLE subtasks (\n1095\t    id           TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- uuid\n1096\t    chat_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,\n1097\t    thread_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,\n1098\t    parent_msg   INTEGER,                   -- message_id that triggered the subtask\n1099\t    prompt       TEXT NOT NULL,\n1100\t    session_id   TEXT,                      -- claude session_id for this subtask\n1101\t    status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',  -- running, done, failed, cancelled\n1102\t    result       TEXT,\n1103\t    error        TEXT,\n1104\t    started_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n1105\t    finished_at  TEXT,\n1106\t    FOREIGN KEY (chat_id, thread_id) REFERENCES sessions(chat_id, thread_id)\n1107\t);\n1108\t```\n1109\t\n1110\t#### SubtaskOrchestrator\n1111\t\n1112\t```go\n1113\ttype SubtaskOrchestrator struct {\n1114\t    db      *DB\n1115\t    sender  *Sender\n1116\t    ptyMgr  *PTYManager  // manages tmux panes for subtask workers\n1117\t}\n1118\t\n1119\ttype SubtaskRequest struct {\n1120\t    ChatID   int64\n1121\t    ThreadID int64\n1122\t    MsgID    int64\n1123\t    Prompts  []string  // one per parallel instance\n1124\t    Group    *Group\n1125\t    Session  *Session  // parent session; each subtask gets its own pane\n1126\t}\n1127\t\n1128\tfunc (o *SubtaskOrchestrator) Run(ctx context.Context, req SubtaskRequest)\n1129\t```\n1130\t\n1131\tBehavior:\n1132\t1. For each prompt, insert a `subtasks` row with `status=running`.\n1133\t2. Spawn a goroutine per prompt; each goroutine launches a fresh tmux pane running `claude` (no `--resume`), injects the prompt via bracketed paste, and scrapes the response via stop-hook or capture-pane.\n1134\t3. As each goroutine completes, update the `subtasks` row and post the result to the originating topic.\n1135\t4. Post results as they arrive (fan-in is non-blocking).\n1136\t5. A final \"All N sub-tasks complete\" summary is sent when all goroutines exit.\n1137\t\n1138\t#### Trigger mechanisms\n1139\t\n1140\t**User-initiated via `/parallel`:**\n1141\t```\n1142\t/parallel\n1143\tResearch the three biggest failure modes in distributed SQLite replication.\n1144\t---\n1145\tList the top 5 Go libraries for distributed locking with pros/cons.\n1146\t---\n1147\tSummarize the WAL mode write amplification problem.\n1148\t```\n1149\tDelimiter `---` splits prompts. Up to 5 parallel instances (configurable per group via `/config max_subtasks N`).\n1150\t\n1151\t**Claude-initiated via tool:**\n1152\tThe bridge exposes a synthetic tool `spawn_subtask` that Claude can call in its stream. When the bridge sees a `tool_use` block with `name=\"spawn_subtask\"`, it:\n1153\t1. Extracts `{\"prompt\": \"...\", \"session_inherit\": true/false}` from the tool input.\n1154\t2. Inserts a `subtasks` row.\n1155\t3. Spawns the sub-task goroutine.\n1156\t4. Returns a synthetic `tool_result` to Claude's stdin: `{\"subtask_id\": \"...\", \"status\": \"dispatched\"}`.\n1157\t5. The sub-task result is posted to the topic when complete.\n1158\t\n1159\tThis lets Claude self-decompose complex tasks into parallel workstreams without the user having to structure the prompt.\n1160\t\n1161\t#### Resource limits\n1162\t\n1163\t- Max concurrent subtasks per topic: 5 (configurable)\n1164\t- Sub-tasks share the group's budget cap\n1165\t- Sub-task timeout: inherits group `timeout_sec`\n1166\t- A topic worker is not blocked while sub-tasks run — the worker goroutine exits `processBatch` after dispatching, and sub-task goroutines post back to the topic via `sender` directly\n1167\t\n1168\t### 7.5 — Background shell job runner\n1169\t\n1170\t**Problem:** Sometimes the user wants to fire a long-running shell process (deploy, test suite, build) and get notified when it completes without tying up a Claude session.\n1171\t\n1172\t**`/bg <command>` command:**\n1173\t\n1174\t```go\n1175\ttype BackgroundJob struct {\n1176\t    ID        string\n1177\t    ChatID    int64\n1178\t    ThreadID  int64\n1179\t    Command   string\n1180\t    Cmd       *exec.Cmd\n1181\t    Status    string // running, done, failed\n1182\t    StartedAt time.Time\n1183\t}\n1184\t```\n1185\t\n1186\tBehavior:\n1187\t- `/bg go test ./...` — launches the command in a goroutine under the group's CWD.\n1188\t- Sends a \"⏳ Background job started: `go test ./...`\" confirmation immediately.\n1189\t- Streams stdout/stderr line-by-line back to the topic (same debounce as streaming, 1s).\n1190\t- On completion: \"✓ Job done (exit 0)\" or \"✗ Job failed (exit 1)\" with last N lines of output.\n1191\t- `/jobs` command lists running background jobs for this topic.\n1192\t- `/kill <job_id>` sends SIGTERM to a running job.\n1193\t\n1194\tBackground jobs are stored in a `background_jobs` SQLite table for persistence across bridge restarts (partially — running jobs are re-marked as `interrupted` on startup).\n1195\t\n1196\t```sql\n1197\tCREATE TABLE background_jobs (\n1198\t    id          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n1199\t    chat_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,\n1200\t    thread_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,\n1201\t    command     TEXT NOT NULL,\n1202\t    status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',\n1203\t    exit_code   INTEGER,\n1204\t    started_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n1205\t    finished_at TEXT\n1206\t);\n1207\t```\n1208\t\n1209\t### New commands summary\n1210\t\n1211\t| Command | Context | Action |\n1212\t|---|---|---|\n1213\t| `/cancel [thread_id]` | General or topic | Cancel the active Claude invocation for a topic |\n1214\t| `/timeout [N]` | Topic | View or set timeout for this topic (0 = no timeout) |\n1215\t| `/parallel` | Topic | Dispatch multi-prompt parallel sub-tasks |\n1216\t| `/bg <command>` | Topic | Run a shell command in background, stream output back |\n1217\t| `/jobs` | Topic | List running background jobs for this topic |\n1218\t| `/kill <job_id>` | Topic | Send SIGTERM to a background job |\n1219\t\n1220\t### Updated architecture diagram\n1221\t\n1222\t```\n1223\t┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n1224\t│                          Bridge (EX44)                               │\n1225\t│                                                                      │\n1226\t│  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────────┐   │\n1227\t│  │  Poller   │→│   Router     │→│      Session Manager          │   │\n1228\t│  └──────────┘  └──────────────┘  │                              │   │\n1229\t│                                  │  TopicWorker (per topic)     │   │\n1230\t│                                  │  ├─ PTY pane (current)       │   │\n1231\t│                                  │  └─ SubtaskOrchestrator      │   │\n1232\t│                                  │       ├─ pane per prompt     │   │\n1233\t│                                  │       └─ fan-in → sender     │   │\n1234\t│                                  └──────────────────────────────┘   │\n1235\t│                                                                      │\n1236\t│  ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐   │\n1237\t│  │  BackgroundJobRunner  │    │  State (SQLite)                  │   │\n1238\t│  │  /bg <cmd>           │    │  groups, sessions, subtasks,     │   │\n1239\t│  │  stdout → topic      │    │  background_jobs, sent_messages  │   │\n1240\t│  └──────────────────────┘    └──────────────────────────────────┘   │\n1241\t└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n1242\t```\n1243\t\n1244\t**Deliverable:** Bridge supports long-running agentic tasks via cancellation, higher timeouts, tool-use visibility, parallel sub-task dispatch, and background shell jobs — all routing output back to the originating topic.\n1245\t\n1246\t---\n1247\t\n1248\t## Phase 8: Dispatcher Architecture\n1249\t\n1250\t**Note:** This was originally numbered as Phase 9 in the original plan. Phase 8 was reserved for a work item that was ultimately merged into other phases. The phase number has been adjusted for coherence.\n1251\t\n1252\t### Purpose\n1253\t\n1254\tThe bridge is primarily a **dispatcher**, not a pipe. Each topic's Claude session is an **orchestrator** — it understands the user's request, delegates parallelisable sub-tasks to **worker** Claude instances, and responds to the user with progress updates and final synthesis. The bridge is the message bus that routes user messages to the orchestrator, worker spawn requests from the orchestrator to new subprocesses, and worker results back to both the orchestrator context and the Telegram thread.\n1255\t\n1256\t### Target architecture\n1257\t\n1258\t```\n1259\tUser message\n1260\t    │\n1261\t    ▼\n1262\tBridge (dispatcher)\n1263\t    │  ──── dispatches to ────►  Orchestrator Claude (--resume session_id)\n1264\t    │                                │  understands request\n1265\t    │                                │  posts \"Starting X workers...\" to thread\n1266\t    │                                │  calls spawn_worker tool N times\n1267\t    │                                ▼\n1268\t    │         ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐\n1269\t    │         │  Worker pool (bridge-managed)              │\n1270\t    │         │  Worker 1: tmux pane, claude (fresh)       │\n1271\t    │         │  Worker 2: tmux pane, claude (fresh)       │\n1272\t    │         │  Worker N: tmux pane, claude (fresh)       │\n1273\t    │         └──────────────────────────────────────┘\n1274\t    │                                │\n1275\t    │         worker completes       │\n1276\t    │         ├─── post result to Telegram thread\n1277\t    │         └─── inject result as tool_result into orchestrator stdin\n1278\t    │                                │\n1279\t    │                         Orchestrator synthesises\n1280\t    │                         posts final response to thread\n1281\t    ▼\n1282\tThread receives: progress updates + individual worker results + final synthesis\n1283\t```\n1284\t\n1285\t### Orchestrator vs worker\n1286\t\n1287\t| | Orchestrator | Worker |\n1288\t|---|---|---|\n1289\t| Session | Persisted (`--resume session_id`) | Fresh per invocation (no `--resume`) |\n1290\t| Purpose | Understand, delegate, synthesise, respond to user | Execute one concrete sub-task |\n1291\t| Model | Configured per topic (default sonnet) | Inherits from orchestrator, or overridden per spawn |\n1292\t| Result routing | Posts synthesis to thread | Result posted to thread + injected back to orchestrator |\n1293\t| Spawning | Calls `spawn_worker` tool | Cannot spawn further workers (depth limit 1) |\n1294\t\n1295\t## Phase 8: Dispatcher Architecture\n1296\t\n1297\t**Note:** This was originally numbered as Phase 9 in the original plan. Phase 8 was reserved for a work item that was ultimately merged into other phases. The phase number has been adjusted for coherence.\n1298\t\n1299\t### 8.1 — Orchestrator system prompt injection\n1300\t\n1301\tThe bridge appends a system prompt to every orchestrator invocation (`--append-system-prompt`) that makes the dispatcher pattern explicit to Claude:\n1302\t\n1303\t```\n1304\tYou are running as an orchestrator in a Telegram Claude Bridge.\n1305\tYou have access to two bridge-provided tools:\n1306\t\n1307\tspawn_worker(prompt, model?)\n1308\t  Dispatches a new headless Claude instance to execute `prompt` independently.\n1309\t  Returns {worker_id}. The worker result will be delivered to you as a tool_result\n1310\t  and also posted directly to the Telegram thread.\n1311\t\n1312\tupdate_progress(message)\n1313\t  Posts a status message to the Telegram thread immediately.\n1314\t  Use this to keep the user informed during long-running work.\n1315\t  Returns {ok: true}.\n1316\t\n1317\tGuidelines:\n1318\t- Use spawn_worker to parallelise independent sub-tasks (research, analysis, code review, etc.)\n1319\t- Use update_progress when more than ~30 seconds have passed without user-visible output.\n1320\t- Synthesise worker results into a final response rather than forwarding raw outputs.\n1321\t- You do not need to spawn workers for simple, fast requests.\n1322\t```\n1323\t\n1324\tThis is injected via `--append-system-prompt` when `groups.dispatcher_mode = true` (default on, opt-out per group).\n1325\t\n1326\t### 8.2 — `spawn_worker` synthetic tool\n1327\t\n1328\tThe bridge intercepts `tool_use` blocks with `name=\"spawn_worker\"` from the orchestrator's stream before forwarding them to Claude as `tool_result`. No actual Anthropic tool definition needed — the system prompt description is sufficient for Claude to call it.\n1329\t\n1330\t**Bridge handling:**\n1331\t1. Parse `tool_use` block: `{name: \"spawn_worker\", input: {prompt, model?}}`\n1332\t2. Insert row into `workers` table (`status=running`)\n1333\t3. Spawn goroutine: launch fresh tmux pane running `claude` (no `--resume`) with the given prompt, inherit CWD, use specified model or orchestrator default\n1334\t4. Return `tool_result` immediately: `{worker_id: \"uuid\", status: \"dispatched\"}` — orchestrator continues without waiting\n1335\t5. Worker goroutine on completion:\n1336\t   - Updates `workers` row to `status=done`\n1337\t   - Posts worker result to Telegram thread: `⚙️ Worker [N] complete: <truncated result>`\n1338\t   - Writes worker result into a pending-injection buffer for the orchestrator\n1339\t6. Next time the user sends a follow-up (or orchestrator posts an update_progress that triggers re-entry), the worker results are injected as additional context prepended to the new prompt\n1340\t\n1341\t**Schema:**\n1342\t```sql\n1343\tCREATE TABLE workers (\n1344\t    id            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,\n1345\t    chat_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,\n1346\t    thread_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,\n1347\t    parent_msg    INTEGER,\n1348\t    prompt        TEXT NOT NULL,\n1349\t    session_id    TEXT,\n1350\t    model         TEXT,\n1351\t    status        TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running',\n1352\t    result        TEXT,\n1353\t    error         TEXT,\n1354\t    started_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (datetime('now')),\n1355\t    finished_at   TEXT\n1356\t);\n1357\t\n1358\tALTER TABLE groups ADD COLUMN dispatcher_mode INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1;\n1359\tALTER TABLE groups ADD COLUMN max_workers INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 5;\n1360\t```\n1361\t\n1362\t### 8.3 — `update_progress` synthetic tool\n1363\t\n1364\tThe bridge intercepts `tool_use` blocks with `name=\"update_progress\"` and posts the message immediately to the Telegram thread without invoking any subprocess.\n1365\t\n1366\t**Bridge handling:**\n1367\t1. Parse: `{name: \"update_progress\", input: {message}}`\n1368\t2. Send `message` to the Telegram thread (new message, not an edit of the placeholder)\n1369\t3. Return `tool_result`: `{ok: true}` — orchestrator continues immediately\n1370\t\n1371\tThis costs ~0ms and lets the orchestrator drive its own update cadence rather than relying on bridge-side timers.\n1372\t\n1373\t### 8.4 — Bridge-side progress ticker\n1374\t\n1375\tIndependent of `update_progress` calls, the bridge posts a heartbeat to the thread when a long invocation is running with no output:\n1376\t\n1377\t- If no Telegram message has been sent for `progress_interval` seconds (default 120s), post: `⏳ Still working… (Xm elapsed)`\n1378\t- Reset timer on every `flushEdit` or `update_progress` call\n1379\t- Configurable per group via `groups.progress_interval_sec` (0 = disabled)\n1380\t\n1381\tThis is a safety net for invocations where Claude never calls `update_progress`.\n1382\t\n1383\t**Schema:**\n1384\t```sql\n1385\tALTER TABLE groups ADD COLUMN progress_interval_sec INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 120;\n1386\t```\n1387\t\n1388\t### 8.5 — Worker result injection on next prompt\n1389\t\n1390\tWhen the user sends a follow-up message while workers are still running (or just completed), the bridge prepends the worker results to the new prompt before sending to the orchestrator:\n1391\t\n1392\t```\n1393\t[Worker results from previous invocation]\n1394\tWorker 1 (analyze X): <result>\n1395\tWorker 2 (check Y): <result>\n1396\t\n1397\t[User message]\n1398\t<user message text>\n1399\t```\n1400\t\n1401\tWorkers complete asynchronously — results accumulate in `pendingWorkerResults` map keyed by `(chatID, threadID)`. The next `processBatch` drains and prepends them. This closes the loop: the orchestrator always has access to worker outputs without needing to poll.\n1402\t\n1403\t### 8.6 — Per-topic dispatcher opt-out\n1404\t\n1405\tSome topics should remain in direct mode (no system prompt injection, no worker spawning). Add `/dispatch [on|off]` command to toggle `sessions.dispatcher_mode` per topic, overriding the group default.\n1406\t\n1407\t**Deliverable:** Bridge is a true dispatcher. Orchestrator Claude instances coordinate worker instances. User sees real-time progress updates and individual worker results as they complete, followed by a synthesised final response.\n1408\t\n1409\t---\n1410\t\n1411\t## Additional Implemented Features\n1412\t\n1413\tThe following features were implemented during development but were not part of the original plan:\n1414\t\n1415\t### Natural Language Intent Detection (Beyond Model
